en: Heating an aerosol spray can increases gas pressure inside, which can make the metal container explode and injure people nearby.
Carbon dioxide gas is denser than oxygen, so it sinks to the floor during a fire, meaning you must crawl low to breathe safer air.
Mixing liquid bleach with acidic toilet bowl cleaners produces toxic chlorine gas, so you must never combine these household cleaning products.
Dissolving oral rehydration salts in clean water creates a specific solution that helps the intestines absorb fluids faster than drinking plain water.
Metals conduct heat rapidly, which is why cooking pots have handles made of wood or plastic to prevent burning your hands.
Chewing food physically breaks it into smaller pieces, increasing the surface area so digestive chemicals in your stomach can break it down faster.
Shaking oil and water creates a temporary mixture, but the oil quickly floats to the top because it is less dense than water.
Water expands when it freezes into solid ice, which is why leaving a sealed glass bottle of water in the freezer can shatter the glass.
Sugar acts as a preservative in fruit jams by binding to the liquid water, which prevents bacteria from growing and spoiling the food.
Friction between car tires and the road generates heat, which physically changes the solid rubber and causes the tires to wear down over time.
Solid dry ice sublimates directly into cold carbon dioxide gas, making it ideal for keeping vaccines cold during transport without leaving wet puddles.
Copper and aluminum are excellent conductors of electricity, which is why electrical wires use these metals wrapped in rubber to prevent dangerous electric shocks.
